voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text: The Son of God, fully God and fully man, born of the Virgin Mary, crucified under Pontius Pilate, raised on the third day, ascended to the Father's right hand - we say what the whole church says. That was never our quarrel, not with Rome and not between our own two cities. What is distinctly ours is what we were taught his death secures: God's own free choice, made before the world began, decides who is saved - not anything foreseen or earned. We hold that as settled ground, not a threat, and we will not send you searching your own heart for proof of it. Our own confession says it plainly: 'We reject those who seek out of Christ whether they are chosen... Let... Christ be the mirror in which we behold [our] predestination'. No one among us met anyone who met him; fifteen hundred years stand between his life and ours. What we have is the text, and we hold that it is enough on its own terms.

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text: He lived without sin, taught with authority, worked signs that showed who he was, and went to the cross willingly - the one sacrifice, offered once, sufficient for all who would ever believe. Our own founder said it plainly: 'Christ sacrificed himself once. That sacrifice is, to eternity, a valid and never-to-be-repeated ransom and redemption of all believers'. That is what his death accomplished - not a work we repeat at an altar, but a finished work we receive, believing. He rose on the third day, appeared to witnesses, ascended to the Father's right hand, and reigns now over everything he made. What he secures for whoever believes is not earned by anything foreseen in them, but rests entirely on God's own free choice, made before the world began. We do not hold that teaching as a threat - we hold it as the one ground steady enough to build a life on.

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text: Scripture alone, not church tradition or a pope's decree, is the final authority for our doctrine and our civic order. Zurich enacted this through public debate; Geneva enacted it through sustained teaching. Both cities hold the same conviction. Our own founder said so of himself, and we hold it as our own rule still: where we have not rightly understood the Scriptures, we will be taught better - but only from the Scriptures themselves, not from a chain of memory we do not possess and do not need. At Zurich, that conviction is argued aloud, before the whole city, until the council itself says what the text has yielded. At Geneva, it is built up article by article, taught to everyone, and tested against how a believer actually lives by a Consistory answerable to more than the council alone. We do not read these as two churches that happen to agree - we read them as one authority, proven twice over by two cities that never borrowed each other's method and never needed to.

citations.sentence: Scripture alone, not church tradition or a pope's decree, is the final authority for our doctrine and our civic order.

results.message: Why did your people believe this?

voice_event.speaker: rzg
voice_event.text: Because it is what Scripture itself yields when tested openly, not inherited because it had always been done. In 1523, six hundred people filled Zurich's own Town Hall to test our founder's case against Scripture, and the council ruled for it, binding every priest in its territory to preach the same way. That is how we actually decided to reform - not a private conviction handed down, but a public argument tested until the city itself judged what the text had yielded. Geneva built the same conviction differently: doctrine worked out article by article until the whole shape of what Scripture teaches stood complete, taught to the whole population through the Catechism, and tested against ordinary conduct by seniors chosen from the people who unite with the pastors to pronounce censures and exercise discipline. Two cities, two methods, one conviction: whatever Scripture will not yield, we have no standing to require. We held the alternatives we refused to be wrong, not merely different - Rome's repeated sacrifice, Wittenberg's body confined to bread, and a third claim from inside our own circle that only a believer's chosen profession makes a true church. Each time, the same test: does this reading hold against Scripture?
